epics.description: Establish AI governance, requirements, architecture, repository tooling, Docker development environment, and database migration foundation.
epics.rationale: A solid foundation is essential before implementing business logic. This establishes patterns, conventions, and infrastructure that all subsequent work depends on.
acceptanceCriteria: AI governance structure is complete and documented
Architecture decisions are recorded
Repository tooling (pnpm workspaces, ESLint, Prettier) is configured
Docker development environment is functional
Database migration system is operational

epics.description: Implement locker domain model, migration and seed data, repository, listing API, and inventory UI.
epics.rationale: Before packages can be stored, the system needs to track available lockers and their sizes.
acceptanceCriteria: Locker domain model supports SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE sizes
Locker migration creates database tables
Seed data provides deterministic locker inventory
Locker repository can list available lockers
API exposes locker inventory endpoint
UI displays locker availability

epics.description: Implement package domain model, allocation policy, pickup code generation/hashing, transactional storage use case, storage API, and storage UI.
epics.rationale: Core business capability: allowing delivery agents to store packages in lockers.
acceptanceCriteria: Package domain model supports all sizes and states
Allocation policy selects smallest suitable locker
Deterministic selection within same size
Pickup codes are cryptographically secure
Pickup code hashes are stored (not plaintext)
Plaintext code returned exactly once
Storage is transactional
API exposes storage endpoint
UI provides storage form and success display

epics.description: Implement retrieval state transition, pickup code verification, locker release, charge policy, retrieval API, and retrieval UI.
epics.rationale: Core business capability: allowing customers to retrieve packages and calculating extended storage charges.
acceptanceCriteria: Retrieval requires locker code and pickup code
Pickup code is verified against hash using constant-time comparison
Successful retrieval releases the locker
Retrieval is idempotent or rejects repeated attempts consistently
Storage charges calculated after grace period
Money uses integer minor units (never float)
Time-dependent behavior uses injected Clock
API exposes retrieval endpoint
UI provides retrieval form and confirmation

epics.description: Implement concurrent allocation protection, database constraint tests, structured logging, health/readiness endpoints, graceful shutdown, and security hardening.
epics.rationale: Level 4 challenge: ensure concurrent requests never allocate the same locker.
acceptanceCriteria: Database partial unique index prevents double allocation
Transaction and row-locking strategy is documented
Concurrent allocation tests verify correctness
Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs
Health endpoint returns status
Readiness endpoint checks database connectivity
Graceful shutdown implemented
Security headers configured
Sensitive data redacted from logs

epics.description: Implement Playwright workflows, CI pipeline, Docker production builds, documentation, interview guide, AI disclosure, and final code review.
epics.rationale: Ensure the project is complete, documented, and ready for interview demonstration.
acceptanceCriteria: Playwright E2E tests cover all major flows
CI pipeline runs all checks
Docker production builds are optimized
All documentation is complete
Interview guide answers all expected questions
AI usage is documented
Final code review completed

tasks.description: Create AI governance directory structure, task management system, initial memory files, and Architecture Decision Records.
tasks.rationale: Establishes the governance framework for AI-assisted development and provides context for all future work.
acceptanceCriteria: .ai/ directory structure created with all required subdirectories
.windsurfrules created with resume protocol and prohibitions
Task management JSON files created (task.schema.json, backlog.json, active.json, completed.json)
Initial memory files created (project.md, domain.md, architecture.md, conventions.md)
Initial ADRs created (modular monolith, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, REST API, feature-oriented React)
Sprint 1 summary created in sprints/sprint-01.md
First session log entry created
NEXT.md updated with next task

tasks.description: Document product requirements, explicit assumptions, domain rules, and API contracts.
tasks.rationale: Clarifies the scope and boundaries of the challenge, especially where the brief is ambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md contains entities, value objects, invariants, and state transitions
docs/API.md documents endpoints, request/response shapes, and error handling
Ambiguous requirements are documented with explicit assumptions
Tradeoffs and limitations are recorded

tasks.description: Configure pnpm workspaces, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, and package.json structure.
tasks.rationale: Establishes development environment and code quality standards.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm-workspace.yaml configured with apps/* and packages/*
Root package.json with scripts and devDependencies
ESLint configuration for TypeScript and React
Prettier configuration with consistent formatting
TypeScript configuration for monorepo

tasks.description: Create Docker Compose configuration for PostgreSQL, API, and web development.
tasks.rationale: Provides consistent, reproducible local development environment.
acceptanceCriteria: compose.yaml with PostgreSQL, API, and web services
Dockerfile for API with multi-stage build
Dockerfile for web with Vite dev server
Environment configuration documented
Services can be started with docker compose up

tasks.description: Set up Drizzle ORM, migration system, and initial database schema.
tasks.rationale: Database persistence is required for all business logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Drizzle ORM configured with PostgreSQL
Migration system with drizzle-kit
Initial schema for lockers table
Migration scripts in package.json
Database connection configuration via environment variables

tasks.summary: Domain Size Model and Value Objects
tasks.description: Implement locker and package size value objects (SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE) with ordering and compatibility rules.
tasks.rationale: Size is core to locker allocation policy. Must be modeled explicitly with validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Size enum with SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE values
Size ordering: SMALL < MEDIUM < LARGE
Size compatibility method: package fits in locker
Value objects are immutable and validated
Unit tests for size comparison and compatibility

tasks.description: Implement LockerRepository port and PostgreSQL implementation with findAvailableLockers query.
tasks.rationale: Repository abstraction enables testing and future database changes.
acceptanceCriteria: LockerRepository interface with findAvailableLockers method
PostgreSQL implementation using Drizzle ORM
Query filters by size and availability
Integration tests with real database
Deterministic ordering within size category

tasks.description: Implement GET /api/v1/lockers endpoint with filtering and availability status.
tasks.rationale: Frontend needs to display available lockers for storage operations.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/lockers endpoint implemented
Query params: size (optional), available (optional)
Response includes locker id, code, size, isAvailable
Error handling for invalid filters
API tests verify response shape

tasks.description: Create React page to display locker inventory with filters and availability status.
tasks.rationale: Delivery agents need UI to view available lockers before storing packages.
acceptanceCriteria: Locker inventory page at /lockers route
Filter by size (SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, ALL)
Filter by availability (available only, all)
Visual indicators for locker availability
Loading and error states handled
Accessible form controls

tasks.description: Write integration tests for locker repository and API with real PostgreSQL.
tasks.rationale: Database-level correctness is critical for allocation. Must test with real PostgreSQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration tests for LockerRepository
Testcontainers or test database setup
Test data isolation between tests
Test availability calculation accuracy
Test deterministic ordering

tasks.description: Implement Package entity, StorageAssignment entity, and domain invariants for package storage lifecycle.
tasks.rationale: Core domain model for package storage operations. Must enforce one active package per locker invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: Package entity with reference, size, status (CREATED, STORED, RETRIEVED), timestamps
StorageAssignment entity linking package to locker with pickupCodeHash
Domain invariant: one active package per locker maximum
Package state transitions: CREATED → STORED → RETRIEVED
Unit tests for entity creation and state transitions

tasks.description: Implement cryptographically secure pickup code generation and secure hashing for storage.
tasks.rationale: Pickup codes must be secure (unpredictable) and only stored as hashes for security. Plaintext returned exactly once during storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Pickup code generation with cryptographically secure random values
Secure hashing using bcrypt or Argon2 (not MD5/SHA1)
Constant-time hash comparison for verification
Only hash stored in database, never plaintext
Plaintext code returned exactly once during storage operation

tasks.description: Implement transactional use case for storing packages with allocation policy.
tasks.rationale: Core business operation: delivery agent stores package, system allocates locker, generates pickup code.
acceptanceCriteria: Use case accepts package reference and size
Allocation policy selects smallest suitable available locker
Deterministic selection when multiple lockers same size
Transactional: package, assignment, and locker status updated atomically
Returns plaintext pickup code exactly once
Idempotent handling for duplicate requests

tasks.description: Implement POST /api/v1/packages endpoint for storing packages.
tasks.rationale: API endpoint for delivery agents to store packages in lockers.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/packages endpoint implemented
Request body: reference, size (SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE)
Response includes: packageId, lockerCode, pickupCode (plaintext, once only)
Error handling: no suitable locker available, invalid size
409 Conflict for duplicate package reference

tasks.description: Create React form for storing packages and displaying pickup code.
tasks.rationale: Delivery agents need UI to input package details and receive pickup code.
acceptanceCriteria: Storage form at /packages/store route (or modal)
Input fields: package reference, size selection
Submit button with loading state
Success view showing locker code and pickup code prominently
Warning that pickup code is shown only once
Error handling: no lockers available, validation errors

tasks.description: Implement use case for retrieving packages with pickup code verification.
tasks.rationale: Recipients need to retrieve packages using pickup codes, releasing lockers for reuse.
acceptanceCriteria: Accept lockerCode and pickupCode as input
Find active storage assignment by locker code
Verify pickup code using constant-time comparison
Mark package as RETRIEVED with transition validation
Mark storage assignment as completed
Return package details and calculated charges
Handle errors: invalid code, already retrieved, locker not found
tasks.implementationNotes: Implemented RetrievePackageUseCase with: (1) Clock interface for testable time, (2) ChargeCalculationService with 24h grace period + $5/day charge, (3) Secure pickup code verification using bcrypt.compare (constant-time), (4) Generic error messages to prevent information leakage, (5) Package state transition STORED->RETRIEVED, (6) Storage assignment deletion to release locker, (7) Comprehensive test coverage for all scenarios including security edge cases.
tasks.testEvidence: 13 unit tests passing covering: successful retrieval, locker release, security error handling (generic errors for all failure cases), already retrieved handling, charge calculation (zero within grace, $5 after 24h, multi-day), idempotency/race conditions.

tasks.description: Extract and enhance pickup code verification with constant-time comparison.
tasks.rationale: Secure verification is critical to prevent timing attacks and information leakage.
acceptanceCriteria: Constant-time code comparison
Generic error messages for all failures
Unit tests for verification edge cases
Security-focused implementation

tasks.description: Implement POST /api/v1/packages/retrieval endpoint.
tasks.rationale: API endpoint for recipients to retrieve packages.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/packages/retrieval endpoint
Request: lockerCode, pickupCode
Response: package details, storage duration, charges
Error handling: 400 validation, 401 invalid (generic), 404 not found
Security: Never distinguish between wrong code, already retrieved, or non-existent
tasks.implementationNotes: Implemented POST /api/v1/packages/retrieval endpoint with: (1) Zod schemas for request/response validation (retrievePackageRequestSchema, retrievePackageResponseSchema), (2) retrievePackage handler function with proper error mapping, (3) Security-focused error handling - all failures return 401 INVALID_PICKUP_CODE without distinguishing between wrong code, already retrieved, or non-existent locker, (4) Proper HTTP status codes: 200 success, 400 validation error, 401 all retrieval failures, 500 internal errors, (5) Response includes packageId, packageReference, lockerCode, storedAt, retrievedAt, storageDuration, and storageCharge with amountMinorUnits/currency/displayAmount.
tasks.testEvidence: All 79 unit tests passing. Manually verified endpoint integrates correctly with RetrievePackageUseCase.

tasks.description: Implement storage charge calculation with grace period and daily rates.
tasks.rationale: Extended storage charges incentivize timely package retrieval.
acceptanceCriteria: 24-hour grace period (free storage)
$5.00 per day after grace period (500 minor units)
Calculate at retrieval time based on storedAt timestamp
Round up to nearest started day
Use injected Clock for testability
Return amount in minor units with currency code

tasks.description: Create React form for retrieving packages with charge display.
tasks.rationale: Recipients need UI to input pickup codes and view charges.
acceptanceCriteria: Route: /packages/retrieval
Input fields: locker code, pickup code
Submit button with loading state
Success view: package reference, storage duration, charge amount (or 'Free')
Generic error handling: 'Invalid pickup code'
tasks.implementationNotes: Implemented Package Retrieval UI with: (1) retrievePackage API function in packageApi.ts with RetrievePackageRequest/Response types, (2) RetrievePackageForm component with locker code and pickup code inputs, loading state, and generic error handling for security, (3) RetrievePackageSuccess component showing package reference, locker code, storage duration, and charge (with 'FREE' display for zero charges), (4) RetrievePackagePage orchestrating form and success views with 'Retrieve Another' functionality, (5) Security-focused error messages that don't distinguish between wrong code, already retrieved, or non-existent locker.
tasks.testEvidence: Components created following established patterns from StorePackageForm/Success/Page. All TypeScript types properly defined.
